scope: All eight exact final declarations and axiom reports plus complete mathematical source for the inverse real-coordinate-to-spinor substitution. The existing coefficient norm foundation is reused; only its literal norm definition and the applied substitution theorem were inspected here.
evidence_category: Lean kernel-compiled finite polynomial coordinate change, physical evaluation, homogeneous-degree preservation and whole coefficient L1 contraction.

findings.reason: For independent target variables [z0,z1,w0,w1], the four inverse polynomials are [(z0+w0)/2, -i*(z0-w0)/2, (z1+w1)/2, -i*(z1-w1)/2]. These recover [y0,y1,y2,y3] for z0=y0+i*y1, z1=y2+i*y3 and w=conjugate(z). The -i/2 factors have the correct sign and the second/fourth coordinates use the correct spinor pair.

ksRealPolynomialToSpinor is actual MvPolynomial.eval2 with the coefficient embedding C and these four explicit linear polynomials. Input and output both have Fin 4 variables but their coordinate interpretations are explicitly different. Coefficients may be arbitrary complex numbers; real refers to the original physical coordinate values, not a restriction on coefficients.

The four inverse evaluations are proved by actual complex real/imaginary algebra. eval_assoc composes these equalities to give the exact input polynomial evaluated at Complex.ofReal(y_i) for every physical y. The expanded type uses the original ksSpinor and actual conjugates in the order z0,z1,conj(z0),conj(z1). No radius, nonzero-coordinate or exclusion of y=0 is present.

Each inverse polynomial is homogeneous of degree one, coefficient constants have degree zero, and the pinned homogeneous eval2 theorem gives the same homogeneous degree k for every k-homogeneous input. This is homogeneous-support membership, permitting zero polynomials; no claim of nonvanishing or exact totalDegree is added.

polynomialCoeffL1 is the actual finite sum of the complex absolute values of all coefficients. Each inverse form has two generator terms with scalar magnitude 1/2, hence L1 at most one. Applying the proved actual polynomial substitution nonexpansiveness gives L1(T(P)) <= L1(P) for the complete polynomial, with cancellation safely handled by upper bounds.

The endpoint is a whole-polynomial L1 contraction. It does not compare an output coefficient to the input coefficient with the same exponent, nor does it assert preservation of a separately supplied uniform bound for each input coefficient. Any conversion from individual coefficient estimates to L1 requires the relevant support-count estimate.

No balance condition is required for this coordinate change, and no theorem here states that a transformed polynomial has balanced support. Physical circle invariance-to-balance and analytic-series descent remain subsequent obligations.

Exact weighted substitution estimate and nonexpansive specialization used by the new endpoint.

limitations: The complex MvPolynomial definitions occur in a noncomputable section. This is a verified algebraic transformation, not an executable rational-polynomial implementation.
No invariant-support implication, analytic convergence, complex radius, physical analytic-plus-distance representation or global gluing is established here.
Whole coefficient L1 is the proved norm; per-coefficient or supremum norm claims require separate arguments.
No bit-complexity, certified energy computation or full Theorem T follows from this module alone.
The strict receipt reuses pinned dependency caches and does not establish an isolated source-dependency rebuild.
